source: Wang et al. (2022/2023) Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning - arithmetic
finding: Sampling many CoT paths and taking the most frequent answer beat greedy CoT on all models tested. Gains grow with model size, except where the model is already near ceiling.
quote: self-consistency still contributes significant additional gains with +12%-18% absolute accuracy on tasks like AQuA and GSM8K
limits: Gains tiny where baseline is near ceiling (AddSub PaLM +1.8). Weak models gain little in absolute terms (UL2 +3 to +7). 40 samples means 40x cost.
agent_relevance: S3 GENERATE + S7 SELECT: the base effect is real and large for mid-difficulty reasoning with a single numeric answer.

source: Wang et al. (2022/2023) Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning - commonsense and symbolic
finding: Gains on commonsense and symbolic tasks are much smaller than on arithmetic, and zero for a model that cannot do the task.
limits: Voting cannot rescue a task where the correct answer is never sampled (UL2 letter task stayed at 0.0).
agent_relevance: Budget voting where the right answer has non-trivial probability; expect +1 to +6 pts on non-arithmetic tasks, not +15.

source: Wang et al. (2022/2023) Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning - aggregation ablation
finding: Plain majority vote equals the best probability-weighted scheme. Unnormalised likelihood weighting is far worse. Voting needs no model scores.
numbers: Table 1, PaLM-540B GSM8K: unweighted majority 74.4; normalised weighted sum 74.1; unnormalised weighted sum 59.9; unnormalised weighted avg 56.3. Greedy 56.5. AQuA 48.3 vs 48.0 vs 38.2.
limits: Raw sequence likelihood is a poor correctness signal. Later work (CISC, Soft-SC) shows better weights can help.
agent_relevance: S7 can be plain code counting. No need to trust token log-probs.

source: Wang et al. (2022/2023) Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning - robustness and uncertainty
finding: Voting helps even when CoT prompting hurts, with imperfect exemplars, and with zero-shot CoT. Agreement rate tracks correctness.
numbers: Table 5, PaLM-540B: ANLI R1 standard 69.1, CoT 68.8, SC 78.5; RTE 84.8 / 79.1 / 86.3; e-SNLI 85.8 / 81.0 / 88.4. Table 8: imperfect CoT prompt 14.9 -> 23.4 with SC (LaMDA GSM8K); zero-shot CoT PaLM GSM8K 43.0 -> 69.2 (+26.2). Fig 5: accuracy rises with consistency percent.
limits: Equation-only reasoning paths gain less (LaMDA GSM8K 5.0 -> 6.5) because short paths give little diversity. Calibration is shown in one figure, not as a calibration metric.
agent_relevance: Consistency share is a free confidence signal for the schema (feeds stop or escalate). Keep chains verbose enough to diversify.

source: Wang et al. (2022/2023) Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning - baselines
finding: Voting beat prompt-permutation ensembles at the same sample count (also reported to beat sample-and-rank and beam search).
numbers: LaMDA-137B, 40 paths vs 40 prompt permutations: GSM8K 27.7 vs 19.2; MultiArith 75.7 vs 60.9; ASDiv 53.3 vs 42.7; ARC-c 59.8 vs 57.0.
limits: Compared on LaMDA; sample-and-rank and beam-search numbers not recorded here.
agent_relevance: Diversity must come from sampling, not from rewording the prompt.

source: Wang et al. (2022/2023) Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning - versus fine-tuned SOTA
finding: Unsupervised voting on a frozen model beat a fine-tuned GPT-3 with a trained verifier on GSM8K.
numbers: PaLM-540B SC 74.4 on GSM8K vs previous SOTA 35 (GPT-3 fine-tuned on 7.5k examples) and 55 (fine-tuned plus 175B verifier), per Table 2 baselines.
limits: Baselines are 2021 and weaker; the comparison no longer reflects the frontier.
agent_relevance: Supports the premise: inference-time structure can replace training.

source: Li et al. (2024) More Agents Is All You Need
finding: Independent large-scale replication across task types: accuracy rises with ensemble size, a small model with many votes beats a bigger single model, and it stacks with CoT and similar methods.
numbers: Up to 40 samples, 10 runs. Gains from scaling ensemble: GSM8K +12 to +24 pts, MATH +6 to +10, Chess +1 to +4, MMLU +5 to +11, HumanEval +4 to +9. Llama2-13B at 59% GSM8K beat single Llama2-70B at 54%.
limits: Combined with Debate on code, two failed cases (Llama2-13B and 70B): debate noise corrupts code logic. Token cost grows linearly with ensemble size.
agent_relevance: Confirms the effect outside the original lab and extends it to code (S7 by vote).

source: Li et al. (2024) More Agents - difficulty moderator
finding: Moderator: relative gain from voting is larger for harder tasks and weaker models.
numbers: Relative gain: Llama2-13B 28-200% vs GPT-3.5-Turbo 8-16%; MATH 34-200% vs GSM8K 16-69%. Synthetic difficulty test: gains 4-18% at {I=10,K=2} vs 16-48% at {I=100,K=4}. Hierarchical use of voting lifted 21 to 31%, and GPT-4 K=32 from 35 to 47%.
limits: Synthetic difficulty is built into the task set-up, so the pattern is partly by design. Relative, not absolute, gains.
agent_relevance: Spend vote budget on hard items and weaker base models, not easy ones.

source: Brown et al. (2024) Large Language Monkeys
finding: Coverage (any-sample-correct) grows near log-linearly with sample count over four orders of magnitude, but majority voting and reward-model selection plateau near 100 samples.
numbers: MATH, Llama-3-8B-Instruct: coverage 82.9% at 100 samples -> 98.44% at 10,000; majority vote or RM only 40.50% -> 41.41%. CodeContests Gemma-2B coverage 0.02% -> 7.1% at 10,000. SWE-bench Lite: DeepSeek-Coder-V2 15.9% at 1 sample -> 56% at 250 (SOTA then 43%).
quote: majority voting and reward models) do not possess this ability
limits: Big gains need an automatic verifier (tests, proof checker). Voting is a weak verifier at scale.
agent_relevance: Key boundary: voting selects the mode, not the rare correct answer. For tasks with tests, S7 should run code, not vote.

source: Brown et al. (2024) Large Language Monkeys - cost and model size
finding: Under equal FLOPs the best model size depends on task. A cheaper weaker model with 5 samples beat single calls to stronger models on SWE-bench Lite at over 3x lower cost.
numbers: DeepSeek 5 samples solved more SWE-bench Lite issues than single GPT-4o or Claude 3.5 Sonnet samples, over 3x cheaper. On MATH a smaller model with more samples maximises coverage; on CodeContests a larger model with fewer samples.
limits: Agent framework fixed (Moatless Tools); mid-2024 prices.
agent_relevance: Cost model for S3: breadth is cheap when a verifier exists.

source: Snell et al. (2024) Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally
finding: Difficulty-adaptive compute beats a fixed policy. Search with a process reward model helps hard items and hurts easy ones. Sequential revisions narrowly beat parallel samples.
numbers: MATH: compute-optimal strategy matches best-of-N using about 4x less compute; a small model with test-time compute can beat a 14x larger one on easy and intermediate questions. Beam search (width 4) degrades on levels 1-2 as budget grows but beats best-of-N on levels 3-4; level 5 no method makes progress. About 38% of correct answers turned wrong under a naive revision model.
limits: PaLM-2 base models and a PRM trained on MATH; findings tied to that verifier. On the hardest tier nothing helps.
agent_relevance: Match sampling effort to estimated difficulty (links to the adaptive stopping subfield). Voting alone is a strong baseline but not the ceiling.

source: Wu et al. (2024) Inference Scaling Laws
finding: Proves majority and weighted-majority accuracy converge to a fixed limit set by the model's answer distribution, at an exponential rate. More samples cannot reach perfect accuracy.
numbers: Llemma-7B beats Llemma-34B under sampling until about 128 samples; Llemma-7B with REBASE tree search beats Llemma-34B with standard majority voting at all budgets; 7B matches 34B at 2x fewer FLOPs on MATH500 and GSM8K.
quote: simple strategies like sampling cannot achieve perfect accuracy even with an infinite number of samples
limits: Math only, Llemma and Mistral families, one reward model. Theorem is asymptotic.
agent_relevance: Formal reason voting plateaus: the answer is the mode of the model's distribution. A different mechanism is needed past it.

source: Zhao et al. (2025) Sample, Scrutinize and Scale
finding: Self-verification over sampled candidates beats voting. Voting saturates and misses rare correct answers.
numbers: Gemini 1.5 Pro, single runs, counts correct. AIME (15 problems): Pass@1 1, Consistency@200 4, Consistency@1000 3, Verification@200 8 (o1-Preview 7). MATH (500): 426 / 460 / 460 / 467. LiveBench Reasoning (140): 63 / 75 / 73 / 97. Consistency@50 equals Consistency@10,000 on AIME. AIME 2024 Problem 11: 1 of 200 samples correct (601); vote picked 1, which appeared in over half.
limits: Each score is one run (cost). Very small sets. Verifier is the same model, and they report weak out-of-box verification.
agent_relevance: Vote then verify: compare candidates across responses. The main upgrade to a pure vote at S7.

source: Chen et al. (2023) Universal Self-Consistency
finding: Asking the LLM to pick the most consistent of N candidates extends voting to free-form output; it roughly matches normal voting on math and execution-based voting on code.
numbers: 8 samples. PaLM 2-L GSM8K: greedy 85.7, random 82.9, SC 90.4, USC 90.2; MATH 30.8 / 28.0 / 37.9 / 37.4. gpt-3.5-turbo GSM8K 73.4 / 68.5 / 78.5 / 77.8; MATH 33.2 / 26.3 / 38.0 / 38.1. ARCADE greedy 42.4, SC-Exec 45.6, USC 45.5. Order shuffled 5 times: GSM8K 89.7 +/- 0.3.
limits: USC stops improving after about 5 samples on SummScreen; limited by context length. Random pick can fall below greedy (GSM8K 82.9 vs 85.7).
agent_relevance: If answers cannot be matched by string, use an LLM judge to find consensus. Where code can run, counting results is still better.

source: Fu et al. (2022) Complexity-Based Prompting
finding: Voting only over the more complex (more-step) chains beats voting over all chains. Voting over the simplest chains is always worse than the full vote.
numbers: N=50 samples, vote over top-K complex chains (K=10..50). GSM8K text-davinci-002: complex prompt 71.5 -> 72.6 with complex voting; code-davinci-002: 82.6 -> 82.9.
limits: Gains from complex voting are small (+0.3 to +1.1). Step count is a proxy that works on arithmetic.
agent_relevance: A cheap code filter before the count: prefer longer, multi-step chains.

source: Lightman et al. (2023) Let's Verify Step by Step
finding: On MATH a step-level reward model beats both an outcome reward model and majority voting. Majority vote is a strong baseline close to the ORM.
numbers: Best-of-1860 on MATH subset: PRM 78.2%, ORM 72.4%, majority voting 69.6%. Out-of-distribution STEM: PRM vs majority AP Physics 80.0 vs 71.7, AMC10/12 86.7 vs 82.2, AP Chemistry 86.7 vs 80.0.
limits: Needs large human step labels. Authors tried combining RM-weighted voting with the PRM and it did not noticeably help.
agent_relevance: A verifier beats a vote when one exists, but a trained PRM is outside our no-training rule.

source: Aggarwal et al. (2023) Adaptive-Consistency
finding: Stopping when a Dirichlet-based test says the leader is safe cuts samples with almost no accuracy loss.
numbers: 17 datasets, 3 LLMs. Up to 7.9x fewer samples, average 3.3x, average accuracy drop below 0.1%.
limits: Needs answers that match exactly; little help when answers are spread out (see Soft-SC).
agent_relevance: Use sequential stopping inside the vote: draw a few, stop on a clear majority.

source: Li et al. (2024) Early-Stopping Self-Consistency (ESC)
finding: Stopping when a small window (size 5 in the example) of samples all agree saves most of the samples at comparable accuracy.
numbers: Average samples cut: MATH -33.8%, GSM8K -80.1%, StrategyQA -76.8%, CommonsenseQA -78.5%, Coin Flip -84.2%, Last Letters -67.4%.
limits: Savings are smallest on the hardest task (MATH). Window size trades cost against accuracy.
agent_relevance: Independent confirmation that cheap early stop works, though savings shrink exactly where voting matters most.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Soft Self-Consistency
finding: Exact-match voting fails in agent tasks with many different valid actions. Scoring by model likelihood works better.
numbers: CodeLlama-34B, k=10, 3 seeds: Soft-SC beats SC by 4.2% on average across datasets; Bash +1.3%, WebShop +6.6%, ALFWorld +4.7%. Soft-SC rises 8.8% on Bash from 7B to 70B vs 5.8% for SC. WebShop over greedy: Soft-SC +8.6%, SC only +2% (as stated in the text).
limits: Needs token likelihoods. Tested on action sequences with open models and some GPT-4 runs.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition: when answers are free-form actions, a plain count has little signal. Use semantic grouping or a judge.

source: Taubenfeld et al. (2025) Confidence Improves Self-Consistency (CISC)
finding: Weighting votes by the model's own confidence cuts the samples needed by over 40% on average. The best-calibrated confidence method was the least useful.
numbers: 9 models, 4 datasets. Gemma2-9B on MATH: CISC with 8 samples beats 30-sample SC.
limits: Needs the model to judge itself. What counts is ranking within one question, not overall calibration.
agent_relevance: Ask for a confidence number with each sample and use it to weight the vote.

source: DeepSeek-AI (2025) DeepSeek-R1, majority voting discussion
finding: For non-reasoning models, voting barely closes the gap to reasoning models. For reasoning models voting still adds a few points.
numbers: GPT-4o AIME 2024: 9.3% -> 13.4% with 64-sample majority vote, vs R1 79.8% and o1 79.2%. R1 Pass@64 is 90.0%; majority voting lifts R1 from 79.8% to 86.7%.
limits: Their explanation (independent samples, no backtracking) is argued, not tested.
agent_relevance: Voting complements long deliberate reasoning; it does not replace it.

source: Muennighoff et al. (2025) s1
finding: Parallel majority voting on the base model did not catch up with sequential budget forcing.
numbers: Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, 64 evaluations at temperature 1, majority over 2,4,8,16,32,64 votes, AIME 2024. The s1-32B budget-forcing curve stays above the base-model voting curve (read from Fig 4; exact vote accuracies not in text).
limits: One benchmark. The comparison mixes a fine-tuned model with a base model.
agent_relevance: Sequential refinement may beat pure voting. Use both (revise, then vote).

source: Zuo et al. (2025) TTRL: Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
finding: Majority-vote agreement works as a reward without labels, and the trained model exceeds the vote ceiling it learned from.
numbers: Qwen2.5-Math-7B AIME 2024 pass@1 12.9 -> 40.2 (+211%); average +76% across AIME24, AMC, MATH-500, GPQA. Final avg@16 exceeded initial maj@16 by more than 20 points. Vote labels are noisy: a wrong label can still give the right reward ('lucky hit').
limits: It is training, outside our scaffold rule. Needs a model that starts with some skill.
agent_relevance: Consensus is a usable noisy label even when sometimes wrong; supports using vote share as a signal.

source: Kim et al. (2025) Correlated Errors in Large Language Models
finding: Models make the same mistakes, so the independence that crowd voting needs is violated. Larger and more accurate models are more correlated.
numbers: 349 LLMs on 12,032 questions (HF leaderboard) and 71 LLMs on 14,042 (Helm): when both wrong, pairs agree about 60% of the time vs 1/3 by chance. Same provider, architecture or size raise correlation; more accurate pairs correlate more even across providers.
limits: About different models, not repeated samples from one model.
agent_relevance: Mixing models helps less than it seems. Samples from one model share its blind spots, which explains the plateau.

source: Snell et al. (2024) Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally - revisions vs parallel
finding: Sequential revisions narrowly beat the same number of parallel samples under both majority and verifier selection. A naive revision model breaks many right answers, so a final vote over the revision chain is needed.
numbers: About 38% of correct answers were converted to incorrect by the naive revision model; sequential beat parallel in Fig 6 (right) for both selectors.
limits: Revision model fine-tuned on MATH for 4 revision steps; gap is narrow.
agent_relevance: If we revise, keep the earlier answers and vote over the chain so a good answer is not lost.
